title: Keyboard Manager: Bugs in the new update

status.label: Confirm target type and current behavior
status.detail: The original shortcut breakage is no longer reported; the remaining launch failure involves a batch-script target.

judgment.rationale: The reporter says the old shortcuts work again and narrows the remaining problem to an application absent from Browse and a failed manually entered path. The attached report shows a .bat target reaching the launch path but not starting. Current new-editor Browse deliberately filters to .exe, so the remaining decision is whether script targets are intended to be supported or an executable launch is still broken.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.98.0 and Windows 11 Home.
The March 24 follow-up says the old shortcuts now work, but the desired target is missing from Browse and fails when its path is entered manually.
The attached diagnostics show the attempted target uses a .bat extension and the launch attempt fails with the generic application-started warning.
The current new-editor file picker filters to .exe; the issue is open and unassigned, with no outstanding maintainer request to the reporter.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the target file type, whether it runs outside Keyboard Manager, and whether the failure remains on the current stable release before choosing script support or executable-launch work.

fix_assessment.rationale: The picker excludes non-.exe targets, while the report shows a manually entered batch-script path reaching the launcher and failing. The intended supported-target contract is not yet explicit, so the likely fix is either a supported script launch path or clear validation rather than an unhelpful generic failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Clarify and handle script targets in app remappings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The new editor picker offers only .exe files, but manually entered paths can reach the launcher without a clear supported-type check. A .bat target therefore appears selectable by path but may fail as though it were a standalone executable.
plan: Confirm whether Keyboard Manager app remappings are intended to support scripts as well as executable files.
If scripts are supported, add an explicit launch path that preserves quoting, arguments, working directory, and the existing elevation behavior.
If scripts are not supported, validate manually entered paths and explain the supported target types instead of returning a generic launch failure.
Add focused editor and engine coverage for executable selection and the chosen script-target behavior.
verification: Verify that an executable can still be selected in Browse and launched by its remapping.
Verify that a batch-script target either launches through the supported path or receives a clear validation message before runtime.
Confirm the existing already-running and elevation settings remain unchanged for supported executable targets.

confidence.rationale: The picker filter and failed script launch are evidenced, but reporter confirmation is needed to distinguish an unsupported target type from a current executable-path regression.

issue_context.summary: The shortcut mappings recovered after the update, but one desired app target is absent from Browse and fails when entered manually; diagnostics identify a batch-script target.
known_information: The issue initially reported PowerToys 0.98.0 on Windows 11 Home.
The reporter later said the shortcut mappings were working properly again.
The remaining report is that the desired target is missing from Browse and does not launch when its path is entered manually.
The attached report records a failed launch attempt for a .bat target; no private path is repeated here.
Current new-editor Browse filters to .exe, and the issue has no assignee.
inferences: The current Browse behavior explains why a batch script is not listed, but the report does not establish whether script launching is intended to be supported.
The generic launch failure may reflect an unsupported script type or a separate path/launcher defect; the current release behavior has not been confirmed.
issue_context.analysis: The broad claim that the update broke all shortcuts is superseded by the reporter's follow-up. The remaining issue is narrower: the picker is executable-only, while a manually supplied batch-script path fails. Confirming target type, direct launch behavior, and current-version reproduction will decide whether to add script support or fix an executable launch regression.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and the reporter's follow-up; confirmed the old shortcut failure is no longer reported and the current ask is the missing/non-launching target.
Reviewed the attached diagnostics privately; the target extension is .bat and the process launch attempt fails. No private directory or filename is included in this artifact.
Read current-main UnifiedMappingControl.xaml.cs: the Browse picker filters to .exe.
Read current-main KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp: the run-program path is expanded and a failed process start produces the generic application-started warning.
Checked current assignees and discussion; the issue is open and unassigned, and the attached report already supplies diagnostics.

information_gaps.information: Whether the intended target is a batch script and whether it launches directly outside Keyboard Manager
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes an unsupported script target from a Keyboard Manager launch failure for a supported executable.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the target extension and whether opening the same file directly from Explorer succeeds; do not include a private path.

information_gaps.information: Whether the manual-path failure persists on current stable PowerToys
information_gaps.why_needed: The supplied report is from 0.98.0, so a later fix may already have changed the launch behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Test on v0.102.3001 or later stable and state the exact PowerToys version and result.

comment.body:
Thanks for the follow-up that the existing shortcuts now work and for including the attached report. The remaining launch attempt is for a `.bat` target, while the current new-editor Browse picker filters to `.exe`; the typed target reaches the launcher but does not start.

Please confirm:
1. Is a batch script the intended target, and does that same file open successfully when launched directly from Explorer? Please do not include its private path.
2. Does the manual-path failure still occur on current stable PowerToys (v0.102.3001 or later)? If so, include the exact PowerToys version.

This will distinguish a script-support gap from a current executable-launch regression. The report already attached is sufficient; there is no need to upload it again.
